name: Calendly

verdict.topBlocker: Strict PKCE enforcement with S256 method on every authorization request, and correct space-separated scope formatting.
verdict.summary: Calendly provides a self-serve developer portal where you can instantly create and configure sandbox or production OAuth apps. Active effort involves setting up PKCE, redirect URIs, and scopes without any mandatory marketplace review gate for standard usage.

steps.title: Log in to Calendly Developer Tools
steps.detail: Log in to Calendly, or sign up for a Calendly account. Open Developer tools by opening the Profile menu and selecting Developer.

steps.title: Create your OAuth App in the Portal
steps.detail: On the OAuth apps tab, select Create OAuth app. Enter the app name using letters, numbers, hyphens, and spaces only, specify your redirect URI, and select the environment type (Sandbox for development and testing, or Production).

steps.title: Select Required API Scopes
steps.detail: Select at least one scope that your app needs based on the API endpoints you plan to call (e.g., scheduled_events:read, users:read).

steps.title: Securely Save Client Credentials
steps.detail: Copy and securely store your Client ID, Client secret, and Webhook signing key immediately upon creation, as they cannot be viewed again.

steps.title: Draft Privacy Policy and Terms
steps.detail: Draft and host the required legal compliance pages (privacy policy and terms of service) for your application server.

steps.title: Implement PKCE Code Verifier and Challenge Generation
steps.detail: Write server or client code to generate a CODE_VERIFIER and build a CODE_CHALLENGE using SHA-256 for the required PKCE S256 flow.

steps.title: Build and Run Test Authorization Flow
steps.detail: Redirect users to Calendly's authorization page with client_id, response_type=code, redirect_uri, code_challenge_method=S256, code_challenge, and space-separated scopes.

steps.title: Exchange Authorization Code for Access Token
steps.detail: Send a POST request to https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, client_id, code_verifier, and HTTP Basic authentication using client secret.

steps.title: Configure Production Environment App
steps.detail: Create a second app for Production in the developer portal using an HTTPS-only redirect URI when your integration is ready for real customer data.

requirements.note: Log in to Calendly, or sign up for a Calendly account to access Developer tools.
Sandbox environment allows http URIs on localhost, while Production requires https URIs only.
Standard compliance requirement for public integrations handling user accounts.

blockers.symptom: The requested scope is invalid, unknown, or malformed.
blockers.cause: Incorrect formatting of the scope parameter or unexpected characters/separators in the authorization URL.
blockers.unblock: Ensure individual permissions are separated by spaces as a single properly formatted string.

blockers.symptom: Authorization request fails or errors out immediately.
blockers.cause: Missing code_challenge parameter in the authorization request.
blockers.unblock: Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the S256 method and supply a valid code_challenge.

blockers.symptom: Redirect URI mismatch error during auth flow.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri sent in the authorization request does not match exactly with the URI registered in the Calendly developer portal.
blockers.unblock: Verify that the redirect URI string matches byte-for-byte between your code and the app configuration.

claims.text: After you create the app, Calendly shows these values: Client ID : your app’s identifier. Send it in each OAuth request. Client secret : a secret that your server uses to authenticate with Calendly. Webhook signing key : a key that you use to verify webhook signatures . Copy all three values and store them securely before you leave this screen. You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again.
